nodes.title: Salesforce contact import: Contact and Lead list views, read only, on the same CrmClient seam as HubSpot and Zoho. The same preview, receipt, CRM-id idempotency, number-change flag and timed sync, plus a per-org API budget, field-level security reported as unreadable, and DoNotCall read as an opt-out.
Salesforce's standard DoNotCall field is read by default and matched as an opt-out (a workspace suppression, never cleared). The registry's DND status is still never taken from a CRM.
nodes.rationale: decision.2026-10-24.crm-consent-only-where-recorded set reverse_if: 'A CRM adds a standard call-consent or DNC field; then it is mapped by default with its own test.' Salesforce has one (Contact and Lead). An explicit do-not-call recorded by the business is the person's wish, and honouring it is the safe direction.
nodes.reverse_if: DoNotCall proves to be used by orgs for something other than the person's wish not to be called (for example a sales-team pause), and buyers ask for it to be a reviewable column instead.

nodes.title: Salesforce pulls keep to a per-org budget: 1,000 calls per rolling 24 hours unless changed, and never past 90% of the org's own limit as Sforce-Limit-Info reports it. A pull counts first and re-checks before every page, and stops before it would pass either, with nothing imported. The calls a stopped pull spent still count.
nodes.rationale: The org's API limit is shared with the customer's other tools; exhausting it breaks them. A 50,000-record list view is about 29 calls at 2,000 per page, so 1,000 is generous for imports and small against Enterprise orgs' limits. Stopping before a page (not mid-import) keeps a pull all-or-nothing.
nodes.reverse_if: Real orgs show the default is routinely too low (syncs blocked) or that 90% leaves too little for their other tools; then change the default or make the reserve per-org.

nodes.title: CRM HTTP reads run in the kernel's prepare step (and, for the timed sync, before its transaction), and API usage is recorded on the pool, outside any transaction. Storing the upload stays in run().
nodes.rationale: Measured: with reads inside run(), a refused pull's usage rows rolled back with the transaction, so the budget undercounted (the intake-salesforce budget test failed). It also held a transaction open across up to ~30 HTTP requests for HubSpot and Zoho, which tools.ts says prepare exists to avoid.
nodes.reverse_if: The kernel gains a way to commit side records from a failing run(), and prepare's cost (a second integration lookup) matters.

nodes.title: A CRM field the connected user may not read (field-level security) gets no column in the pull and is named on the screen and the receipt as unreadable. It is never imported as an empty value. With neither phone field readable, the pull is refused in plain words.
nodes.rationale: An empty 'Do not call' reads as 'may call' and an empty consent as 'no consent': neither was said. Detection works two ways because no official page could be read: a field missing from the describe, or an INVALID_FIELD from SOQL (dropped once and named).
nodes.reverse_if: Salesforce documents a reliable per-field readability flag that is cheaper than describe; use it instead.

nodes.title: Estimating a pull's API calls once, from Salesforce's default 2,000 records per page
nodes.tried: Count the view, estimate ceil(n / 2000) pages, and check the budget once before the first page.
nodes.broke: Salesforce can send smaller pages (wide records). With pages of 2 in the fake, a pull passed the one-time check and then hit the budget mid-read: still nothing imported, but it failed halfway, which the brief rules out. Replaced by a re-estimate before every page from the pages actually received (the intake-salesforce timed-sync test stops before page 2).

nodes.title: Salesforce import against a local fake: 6/6 server tests (list views, paging, DoNotCall opt-out, receipt budget, FLS unreadable two ways, budget and org-reserve stops, REQUEST_LIMIT_EXCEEDED, timed-sync back-off, tenancy) and the browser flow plus axe at 1440 and 390. No write call reached the fake.
nodes.method: node:test on a fresh Postgres with a local HTTP fake shaped from the README's sources; Playwright 1.56.1 via e2e/run.sh with dev/fake-crm.mjs
nodes.not_verified: A real Salesforce org; whether failed requests count toward the daily limit; the official REST pages (403 to automated access).

nodes.title: The Salesforce response shapes come from search-quoted official text and the jsforce 3.6.3 source, not from official pages read directly: developer.salesforce.com returns 403 to automated access, and the API PDF failed TLS through the proxy. Unconfirmed: that describe omits FLS-hidden fields, the REQUEST_LIMIT_EXCEEDED code, DoNotCall on every org, and whether failed calls count.
nodes.closes_when: One read-only run against a Salesforce Developer Edition org (synthetic data) confirms each shape, or the official pages are read in a browser and the README cites them.

nodes.title: Settings > Integrations still shows Salesforce as 'Stored, not used yet' until workspace sets usedBy 'Imports contacts' and the Import link (requested of workspace)
nodes.closes_when: integrations.ts lists salesforce with usedBy and integrations.tsx links it to /contacts/import?from=salesforce.

events.details: Salesforce contact import built in intake (read only; local fakes only), with a per-org API budget, field-level security reported as unreadable, and DoNotCall as an opt-out. CRM reads moved into the kernel's prepare step. The import preview now counts valid-but-not-callable numbers. Verified: tsc clean; intake 30/30; e2e 75/75; screenshots at 1440 and 390 looked at. Not verified: a real org; official Salesforce pages (403).
